meta.title: MetaMorpho vault (Morpho Blue allocator)
meta.description: MetaMorpho: an ERC-4626 vault that supplies its asset to Morpho Blue lending markets in a curated supply queue and withdraws through a withdraw queue; fees are minted as shares. Held-out case: analysed without analyzer changes. Morpho Blue itself is outside the analysed scope (interface only).

boundaries.reason: Only the interface IMorpho is available; the implementation behind MetaMorpho.MORPHO is not part of the snapshot.

notes: Only MetaMorpho.sol and its transitive imports are part of the snapshot (recreate with scripts/fetch_snapshot.py corpus/metamorpho).
MORPHO is an immutable set in the constructor; no deployment is configured, so it stays an external contract identified by the state variable.

Entry points without asset effects (not shown as operations): MetaMorpho.transferOwnership(address), MetaMorpho.acceptOwnership(), MetaMorpho.renounceOwnership(), MetaMorpho.transferOwnership(address), MetaMorpho.setCurator(address), MetaMorpho.setIsAllocator(address,bool), MetaMorpho.setSkimRecipient(address), MetaMorpho.submitTimelock(uint256), MetaMorpho.submitGuardian(address), MetaMorpho.revokePendingTimelock(), MetaMorpho.revokePendingGuardian(), MetaMorpho.revokePendingCap(Id), MetaMorpho.acceptTimelock(), MetaMorpho.acceptGuardian()
Static analysis: relations describe behaviour the code supports (candidates), not observed executions. Amounts are symbolic expressions.

assets.label: MetaMorpho share

identity.note: Token implemented by the analysed contract itself

assets.description: Token minted and burned by MetaMorpho. Transferable: holders can move MetaMorpho share to other accounts via MetaMorpho.transfer(to, value); the holder of a position may differ from the original depositor. Transferable: holders can move MetaMorpho share to other accounts via MetaMorpho.transferFrom(from, to, value); the holder of a position may differ from the original depositor. Model explanation (claude-opus-5-5): A MetaMorpho share converts at (totalAssets + 1) / (totalSupply + 10^DECIMALS_OFFSET), where totalAssets is the vault's interest-accrued supply in withdraw-queue markets on Morpho (vault asset held idle in the vault is not counted); pending fee shares are minted before every deposit, mint, withdraw and redeem, so prices use post-fee totals.

assets.description: ERC4626 asset passed to the constructor. Model explanation (claude-opus-5-5): The curator or owner sets market caps: decreases take effect immediately, while increases and enabling new markets wait for the timelock and can then be accepted by anyone; it can also schedule a market's forced removal.

entities.label: member of MetaMorpho.isAllocator or curator of MetaMorpho or owner of MetaMorpho

Model explanation (claude-opus-5-5): Allocators (as well as the curator and owner) cannot send assets out of the vault directly, but they decide which enabled, capped Morpho markets hold the funds (reallocate, setSupplyQueue) and can prune markets from the withdraw queue, which changes totalAssets and exit liquidity.

entities.description: Caller restricted by an access-control check to one of several addresses. Model explanation (claude-opus-5-5): The guardian, curator or owner can cancel a scheduled market removal before it takes effect, which is the safeguard against a curator writing off a market's supply.

operations.label: MetaMorpho.multicall(data)
operations.description: Any account can batch several MetaMorpho calls in one transaction; each encoded call is delegatecalled on the vault itself, so assets move only as the batched functions (deposit, redeem, reallocate, ...) move them, with the original caller as msg.sender. It reverts if any batched call reverts. (Model explanation, claude-opus-5-5.)

operations.label: MetaMorpho.delegatecall()
operations.description: Within multicall, the vault delegatecalls address(MetaMorpho) once per element of data, running one of its own functions in its own storage context. operations.label: MetaMorpho.reallocate(allocations)
operations.description: An allocator, the curator or the owner moves the vault's supply between Morpho markets: markets whose target is below the current supply are withdrawn from (must be enabled), markets whose target is above are supplied to (must have a non-zero cap and stay within it). It reverts unless total withdrawn equals total supplied, so funds stay inside the vault's Morpho positions. (Model explanation, claude-opus-5-5.)

operations.label: MetaMorpho.submitCap(marketParams, newSupplyCap)
operations.description: The curator or owner sets a supply cap for an existing Morpho market whose loanToken is the vault asset: a decrease applies immediately, an increase is queued behind the timelock and must be finalised with acceptCap. No assets move, but caps bound where deposits and reallocations can supply. (Model explanation, claude-opus-5-5.)

operations.label: MetaMorpho.submitMarketRemoval(marketParams)
operations.description: The curator or owner marks an enabled market with zero cap and no pending cap as removable at block.timestamp + timelock. No assets move, but after that time allocators may drop the market from the withdraw queue even if the vault still supplies there. (Model explanation, claude-opus-5-5.)

conditions.text: reverts if sender != curator && sender != owner()

operations.label: MetaMorpho.setSupplyQueue(newSupplyQueue)
operations.description: An allocator, the curator or the owner replaces the supply queue with up to MAX_QUEUE_LENGTH markets that all have a non-zero cap. No assets move now; the order decides which markets receive future deposits. (Model explanation, claude-opus-5-5.)

conditions.text: reverts if ! isAllocator[sender] && sender != curator && sender != owner()

operations.label: MetaMorpho.updateWithdrawQueue(indexes)
operations.description: An allocator, the curator or the owner reorders the withdraw queue; each market left out must have zero cap and no pending cap, and if the vault still has supply there its removal must have been submitted and the removal time reached. Dropped markets have their config deleted, so their supply no longer counts in totalAssets and is no longer reachable by withdrawals. (Model explanation, claude-opus-5-5.)

conditions.text: reverts if ! isAllocator[sender] && sender != curator && sender != owner()

operations.label: MetaMorpho.revokePendingMarketRemoval(id)
operations.description: The guardian, curator or owner clears a market's removableAt, so allocators can no longer drop it from the withdraw queue while it holds vault supply. No assets move. (Model explanation, claude-opus-5-5.)

operations.label: MetaMorpho.acceptCap(marketParams)
operations.description: Any account can apply a pending cap once its timelock has elapsed; if the market was not enabled it is appended to the withdraw queue and the vault's existing supply there is added to lastTotalAssets without charging a fee. No assets move directly. (Model explanation, claude-opus-5-5.)

source.snippet: contract MetaMorpho is ERC4626, ERC20Permit, Ownable2Step, Multicall, IMetaMorphoStaticTyping {

evidence.title: Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.multicall(data)
evidence.description: other: Any account can batch several MetaMorpho calls in one transaction; each encoded call is delegatecalled on the vault itself, so assets move only as the batched functions (deposit, redeem, reallocate, ...) move them, with the original caller as msg.sender. It reverts if any batched call reverts.

evidence.title: Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.delegatecall()
evidence.description: call: Within multicall, the vault delegatecalls address(MetaMorpho) once per element of data, running one of its own functions in its own storage context. The target is the vault itself, not external code; what moves depends on which function each item encodes.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:29-29
Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.permit(owner, spender, value, deadline, v, r, s)
evidence.description: approve: Any account can submit an EIP-2612 signature by owner that sets spender's allowance over owner's MetaMorpho shares; it reverts after deadline or if the recovered signer is not owner. No asset moves; the allowance later lets spender transfer or redeem owner's shares.

evidence.title: Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.approve(spender, value)
evidence.description: approve: Any share holder sets spender's allowance over the caller's MetaMorpho shares. No asset moves, but the spender can then use transferFrom, withdraw or redeem with the caller as owner.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:771-785
Model interpretation of MORPHO (IMorpho).accrueInterest(marketParams)
evidence.description: call: During deposit, for each supplyQueue market with a non-zero cap the vault asks Morpho Blue to accrue interest before reading its current supply, so the remaining cap is computed on up-to-date balances. Its effect on assets is outside the analysed scope.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:135-135
Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:670-677
Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:771-800
Model interpretation of MORPHO (IMorpho).supply(marketParams, toSupply, 0, address(MetaMorpho), )
evidence.description: allocate: After pulling the depositor's vault asset, the vault walks the supplyQueue and supplies min(remaining cap, remaining assets) to each market on its own behalf; a market whose supply reverts is skipped by try/catch, and the whole deposit reverts (AllCapsReached) if any assets remain unsupplied. The token transfer happens inside Morpho (unresolved), relying on the vault's unlimited approval to MORPHO.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:704-713
Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:803-807

Model interpretation of MORPHO (IMorpho).withdraw(marketParams, toWithdraw, 0, address(MetaMorpho), address(MetaMorpho))
evidence.description: deallocate: Before paying the receiver, the vault walks the withdrawQueue and withdraws min(its supply, available market liquidity, remaining assets) from each market to itself, skipping markets that revert; withdraw reverts (NotEnoughLiquidity) if the queue cannot cover the amount. The token movement is inside Morpho (unresolved); the parent then transfers the assets to receiver.

evidence.title: Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.reallocate(allocations)
evidence.description: allocate: An allocator, the curator or the owner moves the vault's supply between Morpho markets: markets whose target is below the current supply are withdrawn from (must be enabled), markets whose target is above are supplied to (must have a non-zero cap and stay within it). It reverts unless total withdrawn equals total supplied, so funds stay inside the vault's Morpho positions.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:375-375
Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:376-393
Model interpretation of MORPHO (IMorpho).withdraw(allocation.marketParams, withdrawn, shares, address(MetaMorpho), address(MetaMor)
evidence.description: deallocate: Only when the market's current supply exceeds the allocation target, the vault withdraws the difference from that enabled market to itself; with a target of 0 it withdraws all its supply shares, including donated ones. The withdrawn amount counts toward the total that must be resupplied in the same call.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:394-413
Model interpretation of MORPHO (IMorpho).supply(allocation.marketParams, suppliedAssets, 0, address(MetaMorpho), )
evidence.description: allocate: Only when the target is not below current supply, the vault supplies the shortfall (or, for a target of type(uint256).max, all withdrawn-but-unsupplied assets) to a market with a non-zero cap, reverting if the cap would be exceeded. Zero amounts are skipped.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:789-794
Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:813-818
Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:883-906
Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.setFee(newFee)
evidence.description: fee: The owner changes the performance fee (at most MAX_FEE, and only with a non-zero feeRecipient if the fee is non-zero); before switching, accrued fees at the old rate are minted as MetaMorpho shares to the current feeRecipient, only if feeShares != 0. The mint is a side effect; the main effect is the new fee on future interest.

evidence.title: Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.setFeeRecipient(newFeeRecipient)
evidence.description: fee: The owner changes the fee recipient; pending fee shares are first minted to the previous feeRecipient (only if feeShares != 0), so future fees go to the new address. It reverts if the new recipient is zero while a fee is set.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:741-766
Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.submitCap(marketParams, newSupplyCap)
evidence.description: other: The curator or owner sets a supply cap for an existing Morpho market whose loanToken is the vault asset: a decrease applies immediately, an increase is queued behind the timelock and must be finalised with acceptCap. No assets move, but caps bound where deposits and reallocations can supply.

evidence.title: Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.submitMarketRemoval(marketParams)
evidence.description: other: The curator or owner marks an enabled market with zero cap and no pending cap as removable at block.timestamp + timelock. No assets move, but after that time allocators may drop the market from the withdraw queue even if the vault still supplies there.

evidence.title: Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.setSupplyQueue(newSupplyQueue)
evidence.description: other: An allocator, the curator or the owner replaces the supply queue with up to MAX_QUEUE_LENGTH markets that all have a non-zero cap. No assets move now; the order decides which markets receive future deposits.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:585-589
Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.updateWithdrawQueue(indexes)
evidence.description: other: An allocator, the curator or the owner reorders the withdraw queue; each market left out must have zero cap and no pending cap, and if the vault still has supply there its removal must have been submitted and the removal time reached. Dropped markets have their config deleted, so their supply no longer counts in totalAssets and is no longer reachable by withdrawals.

evidence.title: Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.revokePendingMarketRemoval(id)
evidence.description: other: The guardian, curator or owner clears a market's removableAt, so allocators can no longer drop it from the withdraw queue while it holds vault supply. No assets move.

evidence.title: Model interpretation of MetaMorpho.acceptCap(marketParams)
evidence.description: other: Any account can apply a pending cap once its timelock has elapsed; if the market was not enabled it is appended to the withdraw queue and the vault's existing supply there is added to lastTotalAssets without charging a fee. No assets move directly.

source.snippet: // The market's loan asset is guaranteed to be the vault's asset because it has a non-zero supply cap.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:741-757
Model proposal: identity asset:expr:47d57da7 -> asset:vault._asset
evidence.description: A market enters the withdraw queue only through _setCap, which is reached from submitCap (reverts unless marketParams.loanToken == asset()) or from acceptCap of a cap submitted that way, so the loanToken of a withdraw-queue market is the vault asset. This assumes Morpho's idToMarketParams returns the params hashed into the market id (MarketParamsLib is not shown).

evidence.title: Model proposal: claim pos:any:vault -> pos:vault.MORPHO:expr:47d57da7
evidence.description: Redeeming shares makes the vault withdraw its own supply from withdraw-queue markets on Morpho to itself and pay it to receiver, so a share holder can indirectly obtain part of the loan token Morpho holds for the vault, limited to the vault's supply and the market's available liquidity.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:883-890
Model proposal: claim pos:vault.feeRecipient:vault -> pos:vault:vault._asset
evidence.description: Fee shares are ordinary MetaMorpho shares and redeem accepts any owner, so the fee recipient can burn them through redeem (or withdraw) and receive vault asset like any holder; the reported missing exit looks like a role-modelling gap.

evidence.title: Source cited by the model: src/MetaMorpho.sol:894-906
Model proposal: depends_on pos:any:vault -> ent:expr:eea19e27
evidence.description: totalAssets sums expectedSupplyAssets over withdraw-queue markets, which calls the market IRM's borrowRateView to add virtual interest, so the share price and the fee shares minted on every entry and exit depend on the IRM's returned rate.

evidence.title: Model proposal: depends_on pos:any:vault -> pos:vault.MORPHO:expr:47d57da7
evidence.description: Whether a share holder can exit depends on liquidity: each market's withdrawable amount is capped by min(totalSupply - totalBorrow, loanToken balance held by MORPHO), and the exit reverts if the withdraw queue cannot cover the requested assets.

evidence.title: Model explanation of MetaMorpho share
evidence.description: A MetaMorpho share converts at (totalAssets + 1) / (totalSupply + 10^DECIMALS_OFFSET), where totalAssets is the vault's interest-accrued supply in withdraw-queue markets on Morpho (vault asset held idle in the vault is not counted); pending fee shares are minted before every deposit, mint, withdraw and redeem, so prices use post-fee totals.

evidence.title: Model explanation of vault asset
evidence.description: The vault gives MORPHO an unlimited allowance of its asset at construction and supplies every deposit to Morpho in the same transaction (deposit reverts if it cannot all be supplied), so it normally holds little idle asset; withdrawals pull from Morpho just before paying the receiver.

evidence.title: Model explanation of feeRecipient of MetaMorpho
evidence.description: Receives newly minted shares worth fee x (totalAssets - lastTotalAssets), only when that interest and the fee are non-zero; this dilutes other holders and happens on every user entry or exit and before setFee or setFeeRecipient.

evidence.title: Model explanation of member of MetaMorpho.isAllocator or curator of MetaMorpho or owner of MetaMorpho
evidence.description: Allocators (as well as the curator and owner) cannot send assets out of the vault directly, but they decide which enabled, capped Morpho markets hold the funds (reallocate, setSupplyQueue) and can prune markets from the withdraw queue, which changes totalAssets and exit liquidity.

evidence.title: Model explanation of curator of MetaMorpho or owner of MetaMorpho
evidence.description: The curator or owner sets market caps: decreases take effect immediately, while increases and enabling new markets wait for the timelock and can then be accepted by anyone; it can also schedule a market's forced removal.

evidence.title: Model explanation of guardian of MetaMorpho or curator of MetaMorpho or owner of MetaMorpho
evidence.description: The guardian, curator or owner can cancel a scheduled market removal before it takes effect, which is the safeguard against a curator writing off a market's supply.

evidence.title: Model explanation of skimRecipient of MetaMorpho
evidence.description: Anyone can call skim to send the vault's entire balance of any token to the owner-set skimRecipient; it reverts only if no recipient is set.

evidence.title: Model explanation of MORPHO (IMorpho)
evidence.description: Morpho Blue holds the vault's assets as supply positions; the vault's balance there, interest accrual and withdrawable liquidity all come from this out-of-scope contract.

evidence.title: Model explanation of MetaMorpho share held by Any account
evidence.description: Exits are optimistic: withdraw and redeem skip Morpho markets whose withdrawal reverts and revert with NotEnoughLiquidity if the withdraw queue cannot cover the assets, so a fully borrowed market can delay exits.

evidence.title: Model question 1
evidence.description: The facts contain no flow for MORPHO.supply or MORPHO.withdraw; the code relies on Morpho pulling vault asset through the constructor's unlimited approval and sending it back to the vault. Does Morpho move exactly the requested amount and credit supply shares to the vault?

evidence.title: Model question 2
evidence.description: Share pricing, fee shares and maxDeposit call each market IRM's borrowRateView; a misbehaving or reverting IRM could distort the share price or block deposits and exits. The IRM implementations are not analysed.

evidence.title: Model question 3
evidence.description: After a removal timelock, allocators can drop a market where the vault still has supply; its supply leaves totalAssets (share price falls) and is no longer withdrawable, while lastTotalAssets is not lowered. Is this write-off intended, and can the supply be recovered later by re-enabling the market?

evidence.title: Model question 4
evidence.description: skim accepts any token, including the vault asset or the vault's own share; the facts do not settle whether idle vault asset or shares held by the vault should be skimmable by any caller.

evidence.title: Model question 5
evidence.description: The delegatecall target is address(MetaMorpho) itself, so the unresolved call should resolve to the vault's own functions rather than to unknown external code; confirm whether it should be modelled that way.

evidence.title: Model question 6
evidence.description: The code has one accrueInterest and one supply/withdraw call site in _supplyMorpho and _withdrawMorpho; are the #2 operations duplicates of the same call (for example from try/catch lowering), or a distinct path?

evidence.title: Model question 7
evidence.description: The missing exit for fee shares seems resolved by redeem/withdraw with owner = feeRecipient; confirm that the fee recipient address is an account able to call them.

evidence.title: Model question 9
evidence.description: Supply and withdraw loops silently skip markets that revert, and setSupplyQueue does not reject duplicate markets (the code notes maxDeposit may overstate in that case); the resulting placement of funds depends on runtime market behaviour.

item.text: Owner and guardian functions in the code (setCurator, setIsAllocator, setSkimRecipient, submitTimelock, submitGuardian, acceptTimelock, acceptGuardian, revokePendingCap and others) are not in the OPERATIONS list, yet they decide who can steer funds and how long the timelock is.
